title: Time, Speed and Distance

steps.title: The three-variable relationship
steps.content: Distance, speed and time are linked: distance = speed × time. Rearrange to find speed or time. Keep units consistent before calculating.
steps.formula:
Distance = Speed × Time
Speed = Distance ÷ Time
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
steps.example: A car travels at 60 km/h for 2.5 hours. Distance = 60×2.5 = 150 km.
steps.tip: Write the known values with units before substituting.

steps.title: Find the distance
steps.prompt: A bus travels at 45 km/h for 4 hours. How far does it travel?
hints: Units are already consistent in km and hours.

steps.title: Convert units
steps.content: To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5. Convert minutes to hours when speed is in km/h.

steps.title: Convert speed
steps.prompt: Convert 54 km/h into metres per second.

steps.title: Relative speed
steps.content: When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds. When they move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference.
steps.example: Two trains at 50 and 40 km/h in opposite directions approach each other at 90 km/h.

steps.title: Trace a short-time distance
steps.content: Convert minutes to hours before using km/h.
steps.prompt: A train moves at 72 km/h. How far does it travel in 25 minutes?
hints: Convert 25 minutes to a fraction of an hour.
Then multiply by the speed in km/h.

steps.title: Solve a relative-speed meeting
steps.content: Direction decides whether speeds add or subtract.
steps.prompt: Arrange the steps when two cars move toward each other.
options: Divide distance by relative speed to get meeting time
Read the two speeds and the gap
steps.explanation: Opposite directions → add speeds → time = distance / relative speed.
hints: Meeting time uses the relative speed as the divisor.

steps.title: Relative speed
steps.prompt: Two cars travel in opposite directions at 55 and 65 km/h. Relative speed is:
hints: Opposite directions mean the gap closes faster.

steps.title: Catch the average-speed trap
steps.content: A student averages 30 km/h and 60 km/h as 45 km/h for equal distances.
steps.prompt: Why is 45 wrong for equal 60 km legs?
options: Average speed is total distance over total time, which is 40 km/h
Average speed is always the larger speed
Average speed is always the smaller speed
Equal distances always give the arithmetic mean

feedback_by_option.1: Correct. Times are 2 h and 1 h; total 120 km in 3 h → 40 km/h.
feedback_by_option.2: The larger speed alone is not the average.
feedback_by_option.3: The smaller speed alone is not the average.
feedback_by_option.4: Equal distances do not make the arithmetic mean of speeds correct; times differ.

steps.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 40 km/h.
hints: Compute time for each leg separately.
Add distances and times before dividing.

questions.prompt: A 150 km trip takes 3 hours. Find average speed.
A train moves at 72 km/h. Distance in 25 minutes?
Two cars travel opposite ways at 55 and 65 km/h. Relative speed?
A 120 m train crosses a pole in 6 seconds. Speed?
Equal 60 km legs at 30 and 60 km/h. Average speed?

learning_objectives: Use speed, distance and time relationships.
Compute average speed as total distance over total time.
Avoid the arithmetic-mean trap on equal distances.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Average speed is always the average of two speeds.
common_misconceptions.correction: Average speed is total distance divided by total time.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Opposite-direction relative speed is the difference.
common_misconceptions.correction: For opposite directions, add speeds; for same direction, subtract.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Minutes and hours can be mixed without conversion.
common_misconceptions.correction: Convert units before substituting into formulas.

worked_examples.title: Relative speed
worked_examples.input: Cars toward each other at 40 and 50 km/h
worked_examples.explanation: Add speeds when objects move toward each other.

worked_examples.title: Average speed
worked_examples.input: 60 km at 30 km/h and 60 km at 60 km/h
worked_examples.explanation: Total distance over total time, not the mean of speeds.

company_applications.practice: Convert units and calculate relative speed carefully.
Draw a timeline for trains and meeting problems.
Use total distance over total time for averages.

srs_cards.question: What is the relation between distance, speed and time?
How do you convert km/h to m/s?
Why is average speed not the mean of two speeds on equal distances?
srs_cards.answer: Because the times spent at each speed differ; use total distance over total time.

quest.story: Service-company papers mix unit conversion, relative motion and average-speed traps. Keep distance = speed × time as your anchor.
quest.mission: Master distance-speed-time, unit conversion, relative speed and true average speed.
success_criteria: Choose add or subtract for relative speed by direction.
Compute average speed from total distance and total time.
